title: Senate Floor Debate
subtitle: S.3317 — Border Security and Immigration Reform Act

metadata.laymanSummary: The Senate passed sweeping border security legislation that expands detention capacity, funds additional border agents, and overhauls the asylum process.

data.billTitle: Border Security and Immigration Reform Act — Funding 15,000 new border agents, expanding detention, and reforming the asylum system

speakers.name: Sen. Ted Cruz
speakers.title: R-TX · Senate Judiciary
speakers.quote: The border is not secure. Eight million people have entered this country illegally in four years. Texas border communities are overwhelmed. This bill finally gives Border Patrol the resources, the personnel, and the legal authority to enforce the laws that already exist. It is overdue.

speakers.name: Sen. John Thune
speakers.title: R-SD · Senate Majority Leader
speakers.quote: This is the most comprehensive border security legislation in a generation. It is also a reform bill — it creates faster legal pathways for legitimate asylum seekers and invests in processing infrastructure so we never again have a humanitarian crisis at the border.

speakers.name: Sen. Chuck Schumer
speakers.title: D-NY · Senate Minority Leader
speakers.quote: This bill is a political document, not a border security document. It cuts legal immigration pathways, bans asylum categories the law requires us to consider, and would separate families fleeing documented gang violence. Real reform requires balance — this is a political sledgehammer.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: S.3317 passed 55-44 with six Democratic senators joining all Republicans. The bill appropriates $38 billion for border security, including 15,000 new CBP agents, expanded detention facilities, and a new fast-track asylum adjudication system targeting a 90-day decision timeline. Critics argue it also bars asylum claims from people fleeing gang violence and certain domestic abuse situations.
